sentences.text: Revenue compounded from $37.8 billion in FY2017 [F1] to $67.4 billion in FY2026 [F10], a 6.6% CAGR [F196].
FY2018 net income fell to $3.59 billion [F36] from $9.45 billion [F35] as the initial U.S. tax reform charge raised the tax provision [P79].
Operating margin dropped 11.8pp to 25.7% in FY2022 [D246][F30] after litigation-related charges were recorded to acquisition-related and other expenses [P58].
Revenue rose 17.7% in FY2023 [D280], primarily from revenue contributions of the Cerner acquisition [P48].
Cloud Infrastructure added 13.7pp to FY2026 revenue growth [D645], lifting its share of revenue to 26.9% [D643].
Cloud Infrastructure revenue grew 76.9% [D644] as customers purchased and renewed cloud contracts [P17].
Operating income grew 16.6% [D422] against 17.3% revenue growth [D421], an incremental operating margin of 29.4% [D442].
Diluted EPS rose 34.3% [D425], below net income growth of 36.5% [D423], because the diluted share count rose 1.7% [D438].
Cloud Infrastructure now sets the pace of growth, and its cost base sets the margin path.
Operating margin of 30.6% [F34] sits below the 32.2% window median [D788] and the 37.6% window high [D787].
In FY2026 the R&D line added +1.9pp to operating margin [D444], while other cost lines subtracted 2.1pp [D445], mainly from higher cloud infrastructure costs [P19].
Non-R&D cost lines accounted for 11.0pp of the 11.8pp FY2022 margin fall [D259][D246].
Net margin of 25.2% [F54] trailed operating margin of 30.6% [F34] as interest expense rose to $4.60 billion [X92] on new senior notes [P10].
Operating cash flow of $32.0 billion [F84] rose to 1.88x net income [D408] on higher earnings and customer prepayments [P6].
Capex of $55.7 billion [F94] pushed free cash flow to -$23.7 billion [F104], or -1.39x net income [D409], as capital expenditure drove investing outflows [P5].
Free cash flow margin was -35.2% [D405] against a 26.0% window median [D794] and a 34.7% software peer median [D812].
Net debt widened to $97.6 billion [D414] from $81.4 billion [D367], while the current ratio recovered to 1.12x [F184] from 0.75x [F183].
Net cash was -145.0% of revenue [D415], at the 0th percentile of six software peers [D815], against a peer median of -0.5% [D816].
Financing inflows of $40.3 billion [F124] came mainly from senior note issuance [P4], lifting total debt 39.9% [D440] to $130 billion [D413].
Buybacks have largely stopped while dividends continue [X155][X165], so debt is funding the build-out.
High severity: cash and investments of $31.9 billion [D412] cover 1.3 years of the $23.7 billion FY2026 burn [D419][D418], with capex as the stated driver [P7].
Medium severity over two years: free cash flow was -0.03x net income in FY2025 [D362] and -1.39x in FY2026 [D409], against a 1.06x window median [D800].
Medium severity: net debt rose from $81.4 billion [D367] to $97.6 billion [D414], with interest expense up on new senior notes [P10].
Data quality: FY2026 net income of $17.0 billion [F44] is proxy-sourced, while the 10-K reports $17.1 billion [X20], a gap of up to 0.60% [R5].
Capex intensity was 82.6% of revenue [D404], against 37.0% in FY2025 [D357]; a move back toward 37.0% in the FY2027 10-K would confirm the build-out is peaking.
Net cash of -145.0% of revenue [D415] would be reversed if it improves in the FY2027 10-K as cash generation catches up with capex.
Operating margin holding at or above 30.6% [F34] as cloud infrastructure scales would confirm the trend; a fall toward the 25.7% window low [D786] would reverse it.
